title: Oven-Baked Eggs in Ramekins with Creamed Spinach
changes_from_base: Same water-bath baked eggs with a layer of creamed spinach, shallot, nutmeg and hard cheese under the eggs in place of plain cream.
summary: A heartier version of the classic baked eggs in ramekins: the same water-bath method, but the eggs sit in a nest of creamed spinach with shallot, nutmeg and hard cheese instead of plain cream. Baked until the yolks are fully set and served with toast.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Oven, kettle, ramekins
steps.text: This follows the classic baked-egg method, with creamed spinach replacing the plain cream. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and boil a kettle. Grease the ramekins with a little of the butter and stand them in the deep roasting tin.

steps.title: Soften the shallot
steps.text: Melt the remaining butter in the large frying pan over medium heat and cook the shallot for 3 minutes until soft and translucent. Cooking it first takes away its raw sharpness so it blends sweetly into the sauce.

steps.title: Wilt and squeeze
steps.text: Add the spinach in batches, stirring for 2-3 minutes until it has all wilted, then tip it into the colander and press out the liquid firmly. Spinach holds a surprising amount of water, and removing it keeps the filling thick so it does not flood the ramekins.

steps.title: Make it creamy
steps.text: Return the spinach to the pan with the cream and nutmeg and simmer for 1-2 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the cheese, which melts into the cream and helps bind the spinach together.

steps.title: Nest the eggs
steps.text: Divide the spinach among the ramekins and press a hollow into the centre of each with a spoon. Crack 2 eggs into each hollow and season with the salt. The hollow keeps the eggs in the middle, where they bake evenly.

steps.title: Bake in water
steps.text: Pour hot water from the kettle into the tin to come halfway up the ramekins. Bake for 16-20 minutes, checking from 14 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are fully set with no liquid yolk (71 °C in the centre of the yolk); deeper ramekins take longer.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Lift the ramekins out with oven gloves onto plates, as they will be very hot. Grind over the pepper and serve with fingers of toast for dipping into the spinach.

tips: A common mistake is leaving the spinach wet; press it hard in the colander or the filling turns watery and the eggs take longer to set.
Choose an animal-rennet-free Parmesan-style hard cheese and check the label.
Grate the nutmeg sparingly if using whole; a little lifts the spinach, too much tastes medicinal.
The spinach base can be made a few hours ahead and chilled, then filled and baked when needed, allowing a couple of extra minutes.
storage: Best eaten freshly baked. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour, use within 1 day and reheat until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
